tldr: The boundary causal target is the difference of the unique Lipschitz traces of the two observed-side regression classes on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\), so it is an observed-law functional even when conditional means at null boundary points are undefined. A single worst-point thickness modulus does not determine expected-sup difficulty: explicit circular designs with the same two-sided mass order \(h^{\kappa}\) but isolated versus pervasive thin-site multiplicity have rates \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). A count-qualified estimator matches the pervasive frontier without knowing \(\kappa\), and an explicit globally calibrated band has finite-sample simultaneous coverage and matched pervasive global expected-sup half-width. The focal packing profile \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) is declared on \(u\in[0,\infty)\): because local masses are at most one, thresholds \(u\ge1\) simply select all of \(\mathcal B\), while all declared lower--upper profile comparisons remain restricted to \(u\in[0,1]\). Uniform local-oracle width adaptation over arbitrary triangular unions and an exact score-law distinguishability criterion remain open.
gap: Distance-based boundary-curve theory assumes positive design density. Existing random-design sup-norm theory provides unknown-density spatial normalization and inhomogeneous bands under positive continuous univariate density, while degenerate-design theory is pointwise, univariate uniform, or global \(L^2\) with finitely many zeros. These literatures do not identify how the number of thin boundary locations changes expected-sup causal-curve risk.
fill: The project defines the target through unique Lipschitz representatives on restricted-score supports, constructs explicit symmetric circular witnesses and legal two-sided tent families, proves a same-modulus rate separation, and poses both the general frontier and a quantified honest-width problem on named nonempty classes.
